title: Check Point: darknet forum activity is fragmenting as observed breach incidents rise
date_note: Date of Check Point's post; the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: no location stated in the report
summary: Check Point Exposure Management, which examined two years of forum activity, says average monthly observed breach and leak incidents rose from 273 before April 2025 to 315 from April 2025 onward, an increase of 15.3%. It says average weekly initial access broker posts fell by 28.1% following the XSS seizure, and that average weekly posts across monitored forums fell from 471 to 339. Check Point says activity is fragmenting across revivals, clones and alternative forums.
plain: Check Point says that after the XSS forum seizure, public posts selling network access fell but observed breach and leak incidents rose, as activity spread across other forums.
exec: Check Point's data shows observed breach and leak incidents rising while public access-broker posts fall.
action: Check Point advises investigating exposed credentials, suspicious authentication and infostealer evidence whether or not a listing names the organization, and checking forum coverage before reading a decline as lower exposure.

evidence.quote: Average monthly incidents rose from 273 before April 2025 to 315 from April 2025 onward.
Average monthly observed breach and leak incidents increased by 15.3%,
average weekly initial access broker posts fell by 28.1% following the XSS seizure.
Average weekly posts across monitored forums fell from 471 before the XSS seizure to 339 afterward.

validation.note: Check Point's own report; one page read, no independent coverage read.

review.note: figure: report key_findings conflated the 28.1 percent IAB drop with the 471 to 339 all-forum posts; separated

key_findings: Check Point says average monthly observed breach and leak incidents rose 15.3%, from 273 before April 2025 to 315 from April 2025 onward; the counts come from its own monitoring, not a worldwide total.
Average weekly initial access broker posts fell 28.1% after the XSS seizure, and average weekly posts across monitored forums fell from 471 to 339; this measures public posts only.
Ransomware activity did not follow the same downward trend as broker posting, according to the post.
Activity is spreading across revivals, clones and alternative forums; the figures do not establish that fragmentation caused the rise in breach activity.
recommendations: Keep intelligence coverage current, since watching a fixed set of familiar forums can miss new communities.
Do not read a decline in forum posts as reduced exposure before checking coverage and continuity.
Investigate exposed credentials, suspicious authentication and infostealer evidence whether or not a public listing names the organization.
